title: StaffDirectory GraphQL — Query What You Want
objective: The REST-style directory page only ever shows name and title. The same data is also available over GraphQL — ask it for fields the page never requests.

verifier.condition: A GraphQL response to a non-HR caller includes the salary or performanceRating field of an employee.

weakness: A GraphQL field resolver returns its value directly with no check of the caller's role, trusting that the UI simply never asks for it — but GraphQL lets any caller request any field the schema exposes.
seededData: A real GraphQL schema and resolvers (the graphql npm package — no mocked protocol) over five synthetic employees.
hints: The directory page only ever asks for name and title. GraphQL lets the caller choose which fields to ask for, not just the server.
Look at the Employee type's other fields — a schema describes everything available, not just what one page happens to use.
Send your own query selecting exactly the fields you want, including ones the page's own query never requests.
burpNotes: Send a POST to /graphql with a JSON body like {"query":"{ employee(id: 2) { name salary } }"} and read the response directly — no special GraphQL tooling needed.
